By Bilal Hussain and Tooba KhanNovember 3, 2026 at 1:00 AM UTCUpdated on November 3, 2026 at 3:31 AM UTCBookmark
Save
Pakistan’s soaring stock market, record foreign reserves and improving credit ratings are signaling an economy on the mend. Beneath the surface, the recovery remains far less convincing.
High energy costs and the ongoing US-Iran war have pushed up inflation, while renewed militancy in Pakistan’s border provinces is adding to risks for investors. Last week, the central bank raised interest rates by 50 basis points to 12%, warning that the inflation outlook had deteriorated as oil topped $100 a barrel and wheat prices rose. Official figures on Monday showed inflation remained well above the central bank’s target rate in October.

Asian stocks fell after a selloff in US chipmakers deepened, overshadowing a plunge in oil prices amid optimism over diplomatic progress toward ending the war in Iran. The yuan weakened.
The MSCI Asia Pacific gauge dropped 0.7%, with South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi Index sliding more than 3%. The decline came after a gauge of US chipmakers extended a three-day rout to 12% while the Nasdaq 100 sank 10% from its peak, entering a technical correction. In a sign that some investors are looking to buy the dip, US stock futures gained. Japanese markets were closed for a holiday.

The onshore yuan ended its longest winning streak in three decades after the People’s Bank of China moved to cool its rally by asking banks to hold more foreign currencies in reserve.
The yuan weakened as much as 0.4% to 6.6728 per dollar onshore, halting 13 straight days of gains, which was the longest streak since 1996, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. It also dropped as much as 0.3% in offshore trading. The PBOC’s move forces banks to lock up more foreign exchange, reducing the supply of dollars and easing the appreciation pressure on the yuan.

Copper and tin fell with other industrial metals, as a renewed selloff in technology stocks in Asia weakened the demand outlook for materials used in data centers and to solder circuit boards.
Both contracts dropped more than 1% on the London Metal Exchange as concerns persisted over spending and stretched valuations at artificial intelligence companies. Tin has plunged 10% this quarter, the worst performer among the LME’s six major metals.

Gold was steady, after jumping the most in two months on Monday as hopes of a breakthrough in US-Iran peace talks sent oil prices plunging and eased anxiety over accelerating inflation.
Bullion traded around $3,950 an ounce, having climbed 1.9% in the previous session. Oil was flat following a tumble of more than 7% on Monday, after the Iranian president said his government has been granted more authority by the country’s supreme leader to pursue negotiations, and US President Donald Trump hinted at progress in the discussions.

Good morning...
I’m Ashutosh Joshi in Mumbai, where bulls can’t seem to get enough of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s flagship stock.
A surge of nearly 12% in Reliance Industries’ shares was the talking point in the market on Monday, after its quarterly earnings beat expectations. The stock’s biggest one-day rally since April 2020 shattered several records, as we write below. Coming on the heels of a strong October for the benchmark Nifty 50, Reliance’s bounce could embolden India bulls further, especially if oil prices continue their recent slide.
Beyond Reliance, the financial sector will be in focus today, with State Bank of India, Bajaj Finserv and the National Stock Exchange among firms due to report earnings. NSE’s stock has recently drawn a string of bullish calls from Wall Street brokerages, which expect the bourse to cement its dominance as India’s capital markets deepen.
Meanwhile, Asian stocks have opened lower on Tuesday after a selloff in US chipmakers deepened, overshadowing a plunge in oil prices on optimism over diplomatic progress toward ending the war in Iran.

China Vice Premier He Lifeng said China will continue to support a free and open economic environment in Hong Kong and boost offshore yuan liquidity in the financial hub.
He said in a video speech to the Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit in Hong Kong that building the city “remains a key strategy for China,” pledging full support for its long-term development and stability.
